title: OOM flapping bisect checklist & notes
content:
Quick summary:
- Intermittent OOMs on GPU node pool (rtx-a6000-like machines) while running the same micro-benchmark workload. Flapping: sometimes run completes fine, sometimes OOM after ~6-8 steps. No consistent correlation with input size.

Symptoms and environment:
- Platform image: ubuntu 22.04, driver: nvidia-driver 535.86, CUDA toolkit: 12.1 installed in /usr/local/cuda-12.1, container runtime: docker 24.x with --gpus.
- Framework: PyTorch 2.2 built against cuda11 ABI (packaged wheel). Many teams using mixed conda envs.
- Dataset: deterministic tiny tensors (batch 2, seq len 512). Repro locally sometimes fails, sometimes not.

Observed error snippets (copied from failing runs):
- "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.23 GiB (GPU 0; 48.00 GiB total capacity; 46.55 GiB already allocated; 1.45 GiB free; 1.50 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)"
- "Failed to initialize NVML: Unknown Error" (intermittent at process start)
- dmesg around crash: "NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus" (rare)
- Container startup: "libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory" when LD_LIBRARY_PATH picked up host-nonstandard path

Commands I ran (notes + outputs trimmed):
1) Basic GPU introspection:
- nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY
  -> shows expected capacities on healthy nodes; on repro node sometimes reports 0 for processes list (but memory still high reported by driver)

2) Check lib deps for torch cuda libs:
- ldd $(python -c 'import torch; print(torch.__file__)').replace('\n','') ??? (manual steps):
  - ldd /opt/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so
  -> libcuda.so.1 => /usr/local/nvidia/lib/libcuda.so.1 (OK)
  -> cuda runtime linked to cudart_static? some warnings about missing libnvidia-ml.so.1

3) NVML probes to reproduce init error:
- python -c 'import pynvml; pynvml.nvmlInit(); print(pynvml.nvmlSystemGetDriverVersion())'
  -> sometimes returns driver version, sometimes raises NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN (stacktrace attached locally)

4) Strace on failing run startup (filtered):
- openat("/usr/local/nvidia/lib/libcuda.so.1", O_RDONLY) = 3
- openat("/etc/ld.so.cache", O_RDONLY) = 3
- writev(1, ["CUDA out of memory"], 1) = 17
- futex(0x...), wait...
(Observation: occasional EBUSY on fopen of /dev/nvidia0?)

5) Repro script variations (toy reproducer):
- baseline: python run_model.py --batch 2 --steps 8  -> sometimes OOM after step 6
- add torch.cuda.empty_cache() between steps  -> reduces frequency but does not eliminate flapping
- run under CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 -> deterministic failure more often (interesting)

6) Docker runtime experiments:
- docker run --gpus all --rm --ipc=host -e NVIDIA_DISABLE_REQUIRE=1 image bash -c 'python run_model.py'
  -> failure rate ~70% on repro node, ~5% on non-repro nodes
- adding --shm-size=1g made no difference; --ipc=host slightly improved stability

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Library/driver shadowing or intermittent ldconfig/ld.so cache mismatch: multiple libcuda copies on host (nvidia-driver + cuda-toolkit) and container sometimes picks wrong one. Explains ld error and NVML init flakiness.
2) NVML / driver transient failure causing driver to report less free memory (NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN). Could result from kernel-level hiccup (oom_killer? pci reset?)
3) Tensor-core/memory fragmentation combined with small transient allocations (allocator fragmentation). PyTorch reserved pool leaves little contiguous memory -> flapping with concurrent kernel launches (continuous batching).
4) cgroup/OCI runtime GPU accounting bug (rare) causing wrong memory cap to be reported to containerized process.
5) Mixed CUDA ABI mismatch (PyTorch built for cuda11 running on cuda12 driver toolset) leading to subtle behaviour.

Experiments performed and outcome summary:
- Force single libcuda: set LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/nvidia/lib and LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/nvidia/lib/libcuda.so.1 -> NVML init stable for longer but not permanent fix.
- Swap driver to 525.x on one test node -> immediate drop in failure rate but not eliminated; logistic issues rolling out driver downgrade.
- Rebuild minimal wheel of PyTorch against cuda12 (local build) -> preliminary runs look stable in short smoke tests (3/3 runs). This points to ABI/compat issue as plausible.
- Increased contiguous shm with --ipc=host + torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction(0.9) had marginal benefit.

Minimal repro recipe (best-effort):
1) Start container with default runtime and env.
2) run small script that allocates and frees random-sized tensors across steps and triggers cuBLAS work between allocations.
3) Repeat until failure. Observed that inserting sleep(0.03) between iterations changes failure frequency. (timing sensitive)

Important command snippets to re-run: 
- python - <<PY
import torch, time
for i in range(120):
    a = torch.empty((1024, 1024, 8), device='cuda', dtype=torch.float32)
    b = torch.empty((1024, 1024, 8), device='cuda', dtype=torch.float32)
    c = torch.matmul(a, b)
    if i % 4 == 0: torch.cuda.empty_cache();
    time.sleep(0.02)
PY

- ldd /opt/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so | grep -E 'libcuda|libnvidia'
- python -c 'import pynvml; pynvml.nvmlInit(); print(pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo(pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex(0)))'

Mitigations attempted in prod: 
- Canary: pinned to PyTorch wheel built against system CUDA 12 (rolled out to 4 nodes) -> observed drop in incidents by ~80% over 48h.
- Auto-retry on OOM in serving path (short-term): implemented graceful fallback and retry with smaller batch.
- Node patch: fixed /etc/ld.so.conf.d entries to ensure single libcuda symlink. Testing ongoing.

Notes / breadcrumbs for next bisect: 
- Prioritize reproducer under the same docker image that's failing in prod (capture docker image id).
- Collect full strace+LD_DEBUG=symbols for failing run (heavy but necessary).
- Capture nvml logs and run nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps to correlate processes at time of failure.
- Re-run with TORCH_USE_RTLD_GLOBAL=1 and with TORCH_USE_RTLD_LOCAL=1 to see if symbol resolution affects crash frequency.

Open questions and TODOs:
- Is there any scheduled kernel patch / node maint that coincides with higher failure windows? (check infra calendar)
- Are there any processes on host intermittently opening /dev/nvidiactl that can cause NVML init contention? (check auditd logs)
- If ABI mismatch is primary cause, what is rollout plan for rebuilding internal wheels vs upgrading drivers?
- Run a controlled A/B: driver 535 + wheel built-for-11 vs driver 525 + same wheel to isolate driver vs wheel.

Notes to self: keep raw traces in /tmp/oom-bisect-<node>-YYYYMMDD.tgz and link them in the ticket. Don't forget to capture dmesg -T and journalctl -k around failure timestamps.

Attachments (local): full strace logs, pynvml stack traces, docker image manifest.

Quick log of timestamps: 
- 2026-02-18: first reproducible flapping observed in staging.
- 2026-02-22: tried LD_PRELOAD hack -> temporary improvement.
- 2026-03-01: built test PyTorch wheel against CUDA12 -> preliminary positive results.
- 2026-03-12: rolled canary to 4 nodes; incidents down 80%.

If I stop here: checklist for next session:
- [ ] Capture full LD_DEBUG=symbols + strace for one failure run.
- [ ] Run the A/B driver vs wheel test on 2 small nodes.
- [ ] Confirm no host-side process is racing NVML access (auditd).
- [ ] Add an e2e smoke test that runs the reproducer on new images during CI before deployment.

End of scratchpad.
